entries.appliesTo: persons making campaign communications that include synthetic media

dutySources.disclosure-ui: § 40 (ORS 260.268(2)) — 'A campaign communication that includes any form of synthetic media must include a disclosure stating that the image, audio recording or video recording has been manipulated.'

exposure.enforcer: secretary-of-state (injunctive proceedings); civil penalty imposed by circuit court

sources.disclosure: § 40 (ORS 260.268(2)) — 'A campaign communication that includes any form of synthetic media must include a disclosure stating that the image, audio recording or video recording has been manipulated.'
sources.scope: § 40 (ORS 260.268(1)(a)(A)–(B)) — '"Campaign communication" means a communication in support of or in opposition to a clearly identified candidate or measure' … 'a campaign communication may involve aggregate expenditures of any amount.'
sources.penaltyMax: § 40 (ORS 260.268(4)) — 'Upon proof of any violation of this section, the court shall impose a civil penalty of not more than $10,000.'
sources.enforcer: § 40 (ORS 260.268(3)) — 'The Secretary of State may institute proceedings to enjoin any violation of this section.' and (4) 'the court shall impose a civil penalty'

flags: Omnibus campaign-finance act: the bill's dominant content (contribution limits ORS 260.014, unexpended-funds limits ORS 260.018, independent-expenditure original-source disclosure ORS 260.059, donor identification lists §§ 23-25, foreign-national contribution ban § 14, disclaimer rules ORS 260.266) has no AI content and fits no family in the coding vocabulary; only § 40 (ORS 260.268 synthetic media) is coded.

§ 40 amends preexisting ORS 260.268; the visible changes are conforming cross-reference updates (e.g. 'as defined in ORS 260.005 [(10)(c)]') — the synthetic-media disclosure regime itself predates this act (chapter 9, Oregon Laws 2024) and is restated here as amended text.

scope enum is lossy: 'campaign communication' covers communications 'distributed via print, telephone, radio, television or the Internet' in support of or opposition to a clearly identified candidate or measure, at any expenditure amount; coded as all-communications.

Exemptions in ORS 260.268(6): interactive computer services/information services (47 U.S.C. 230(f), 153), bona fide newscasts with authenticity acknowledgment, paid broadcasters/platforms, periodicals with an accuracy statement, and satire/parody or non-technological impersonation.
ORS 260.268(5): 'The remedy provided by this section is the exclusive remedy for a violation of this section.'
Injunctions available 'without proof of injury or damage to any person'; prevailing party recovers 'reasonable attorney fees at trial and on appeal' (ORS 260.268(3)).
Operative date: § 42(1) — 'The amendments to ORS 260.007, 260.041, 260.044, 260.083, 260.205 and 260.268 by sections 30, 31 and 37 to 40 of this 2026 Act become operative on January 1, 2027.'
